items.title: Pong
items.notes: The original 1972 table tennis arcade game that launched the commercial video game industry.

items.title: Space Invaders
items.notes: Taito's 1978 fixed shooter that popularized the high-score chase and helped spark the golden age of arcades.

items.title: Asteroids
items.notes: Atari's 1979 vector-graphics space shooter with inertia-based movement.

items.title: Pac-Man
items.notes: Namco's iconic maze-chase game, one of the highest-grossing arcade games of all time.

items.title: Donkey Kong
items.notes: Nintendo's 1981 arcade debut of both Mario and Donkey Kong, defining the platformer genre.

items.title: Galaga
items.notes: Namco's beloved fixed-shooter sequel to Galaxian with dual-ship capture mechanic.

items.title: Centipede
items.notes: Atari trackball-driven shooter with segmented enemies descending through a mushroom field.

items.title: Frogger
items.notes: Konami's traffic-and-river crossing game, a timeless arcade staple.

items.title: Missile Command
items.notes: Atari Cold War-era anti-missile defense game with trackball controls.

items.title: Adventure (Atari 2600)
items.notes: One of the first action-adventure console games and the first known video game Easter egg.

items.title: Super Mario Bros.
items.notes: The 1985 NES side-scroller that single-handedly revived the American console market.

items.title: The Legend of Zelda
items.notes: Nintendo's 1986 open-world action-adventure with battery-backed save, the blueprint for the series.

items.title: Metroid
items.notes: Non-linear sci-fi exploration game that co-defined the Metroidvania genre.

items.title: Mega Man 2
items.notes: Capcom's 1988 NES classic, widely regarded as the best in the original Mega Man series.

items.title: Castlevania
items.notes: Konami's gothic horror platformer series debut on NES.

items.title: Tetris (Game Boy)
items.notes: The quintessential puzzle game, bundled with Game Boy and sold 35 million copies.

items.title: Contra
items.notes: Konami's legendary run-and-gun with the iconic Konami Code for 30 lives.

items.title: Punch-Out!!
items.notes: Nintendo's pattern-based boxing game starring Little Mac.

items.title: Ninja Gaiden
items.notes: Tecmo's cinematic NES action-platformer known for its brutal difficulty.

items.title: Kirby's Dream Land
items.notes: HAL Laboratory's 1992 Game Boy debut of the pink puffball Kirby.

items.title: Super Mario World
items.notes: SNES launch title, one of the greatest platformers ever made with Yoshi's debut.

items.title: Sonic the Hedgehog
items.notes: Sega's blazing-fast mascot platformer that defined the Genesis era.

items.title: Super Metroid
items.notes: The gold standard of atmospheric exploration-action games.

items.title: The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past
items.notes: The SNES Zelda that perfected the top-down formula.

items.title: Street Fighter II
items.notes: Capcom's genre-defining 1991 fighting game that launched competitive gaming.

items.title: Chrono Trigger
items.notes: Square's time-traveling RPG masterpiece with multiple endings and a Dream Team of developers.

items.title: Final Fantasy VI
items.notes: Square's ambitious ensemble RPG, often cited as the finest pre-3D Final Fantasy.

items.title: Donkey Kong Country
items.notes: Rare's pre-rendered 3D graphics revolution on SNES.

items.title: Mortal Kombat
items.notes: Midway's digitized-fighter that sparked the ESRB rating system.

items.title: Earthbound
items.notes: Nintendo's quirky modern-setting RPG, a cult classic that inspired Undertale.

items.title: Super Mario 64
items.notes: The game that defined 3D platforming with analog stick movement and a free camera.

items.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
items.notes: Widely considered one of the greatest games ever made. Z-targeting changed 3D combat forever.

items.title: Final Fantasy VII
items.notes: Square's 1997 RPG that brought JRPGs to the Western mainstream and sold 13+ million copies.

items.title: Metal Gear Solid
items.notes: Hideo Kojima's cinematic stealth-action masterpiece that redefined storytelling in games.

items.title: Resident Evil
items.notes: Capcom's genre-defining survival horror with fixed camera angles and resource scarcity.

items.title: GoldenEye 007
items.notes: Rare's 1997 N64 FPS that proved console shooters could work, legendary 4-player split-screen.

items.title: Crash Bandicoot
items.notes: Naughty Dog's PS1 mascot platformer, Sony's answer to Mario.

items.title: Spyro the Dragon
items.notes: Insomniac Games' colorful 3D collect-a-thon platformer.

items.title: Tekken 3
items.notes: Namco's 1997 PS1 fighter, one of the best-selling and highest-rated fighting games.

items.title: Half-Life
items.notes: Valve's 1998 PC FPS that pioneered scripted in-game storytelling with no cutscenes.

items.title: StarCraft
items.notes: Blizzard's 1998 RTS that became a national sport in South Korea.

items.title: Pokémon Red/Blue
items.notes: Game Freak's 1996 monster-collecting RPGs that launched a multi-billion dollar franchise.

items.title: Pokémon Gold/Silver
items.notes: The beloved Gen 2 Pokémon games with the day/night cycle and two full regions.

items.title: Tony Hawk's Pro Skater
items.notes: Neversoft's 1999 skateboarding game with a legendary punk/ska soundtrack.

items.title: Diablo
items.notes: Blizzard's dark gothic action-RPG that defined the loot-driven dungeon-crawler genre.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas
items.notes: Rockstar's sprawling open-world crime epic across three cities.

items.title: Metal Gear Solid 2
items.notes: Kojima's controversial PS2 sequel with the Raiden bait-and-switch.

items.title: Halo: Combat Evolved
items.notes: Bungie's Xbox launch title that made console FPS mainstream.

items.title: Super Smash Bros. Melee
items.notes: Nintendo's GameCube crossover fighter, still played competitively 20+ years later.

items.title: Kingdom Hearts
items.notes: Square and Disney's unexpected action-RPG crossover.

items.title: Shadow of the Colossus
items.notes: Team Ico's 2005 PS2 masterpiece — 16 colossi, no filler.

items.title: Resident Evil 4
items.notes: Capcom's 2005 over-the-shoulder reinvention of the franchise.

items.title: God of War
items.notes: Sony Santa Monica's brutal Greek mythology action game.

items.title: Sonic Adventure 2
items.notes: Sega's last Sonic game before going third-party.

items.title: Ratchet & Clank
items.notes: Insomniac's PS2 action-platformer with inventive weaponry.

items.title: Jak and Daxter
items.notes: Naughty Dog's PS2 platformer with seamless open-world streaming.

items.title: Devil May Cry
items.notes: Capcom's stylish 2001 hack-and-slash that birthed the character-action genre.

items.title: Animal Crossing
items.notes: Nintendo's real-time village life simulation.

items.title: The Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker
items.notes: Nintendo's cel-shaded Zelda, controversial at reveal but now beloved.

items.title: Metroid Fusion
items.notes: The more linear, horror-tinged Metroid with SA-X pursuit sequences.

items.title: Metroid: Zero Mission
items.notes: A superb GBA reimagining of the original NES Metroid.

items.title: Advance Wars
items.notes: Intelligent Systems' accessible turn-based tactics gem.

items.title: Golden Sun
items.notes: Camelot's GBA RPG with Djinn-based class system and impressive visuals.

items.title: The Legend of Zelda: The Minish Cap
items.notes: Capcom-developed GBA Zelda with shrinking mechanic.

items.title: Fire Emblem (GBA)
items.notes: The first Fire Emblem localized for the West on GBA.

items.title: Mario Kart: Super Circuit
items.notes: Mode 7-style Mario Kart with all SNES tracks included.

items.title: Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow
items.notes: Widely regarded as the best GBA Castlevania with the Tactical Soul system.

items.title: Kirby & the Amazing Mirror
items.notes: Non-linear Kirby with interconnected Metroidvania-style world.

items.title: WarioWare, Inc.
items.notes: Nintendo's manic microgame collection — 5-second challenges at breakneck speed.

items.title: Pokémon Ruby/Sapphire/Emerald
items.notes: Gen 3 Pokémon introducing abilities, natures, and double battles.

items.title: F-Zero: Maximum Velocity
items.notes: GBA launch-window F-Zero at blistering Mode 7 speed.

items.title: Sword of Mana
items.notes: Square's GBA remake of Final Fantasy Adventure / Seiken Densetsu 1.

items.title: Portal
items.notes: Valve's 2007 spatial-puzzle FPS — 'The cake is a lie.'

items.title: BioShock
items.notes: Irrational Games' 2007 underwater dystopia with 'Would you kindly?'

items.title: Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare
items.notes: The 2007 shooter that modernized the military FPS and defined online multiplayer for a decade.

items.title: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion
items.notes: Bethesda's 2006 open-world RPG that pushed next-gen visual fidelity.

items.title: Super Mario Galaxy
items.notes: Nintendo's gravity-defying Wii platformer with orchestral soundtrack.

items.title: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess
items.notes: The dark, mature-toned Zelda bridging GameCube and Wii.

items.title: Uncharted 2
items.notes: Naughty Dog's cinematic action-adventure benchmark on PS3.

items.title: Red Dead Redemption
items.notes: Rockstar's 2010 open-world Western epic.

items.title: Mass Effect 2
items.notes: BioWare's 2010 sci-fi RPG with consequence-driven squad loyalty.

items.title: Left 4 Dead
items.notes: Valve's 4-player co-op zombie survival shooter with AI Director.

items.title: Minecraft (early)
items.notes: Notch's 2009 voxel sandbox — the best-selling game of all time (300M+).

items.title: Fallout 3
items.notes: Bethesda's 2008 post-apocalyptic RPG bringing Fallout into 3D open-world.

items.title: Batman: Arkham Asylum
items.notes: Rocksteady's 2009 game that finally got Batman right in video games.

items.title: Wii Sports
items.notes: The Wii pack-in that brought gaming to grandparents worldwide.

items.title: Dark Souls
items.notes: FromSoftware's 2011 punishing masterpiece that spawned the Soulslike genre.

items.title: God of War: Chains of Olympus
items.notes: PSP prequel showcasing console-quality action on handheld.

items.title: Monster Hunter Freedom Unite
items.notes: Capcom's co-op hunting RPG that dominated PSP in Japan.

items.title: Patapon

items.notes: Enhanced customization, Health Connect, and per-app language settings.

items.title: Android 15
items.notes: Satellite connectivity support and Private Space for sensitive apps.

items.title: iPhone OS 1
items.notes: The original iPhone OS — no App Store, no copy-paste, but revolutionary multi-touch.

items.title: iOS 4
items.notes: First iOS with multitasking, folders, and FaceTime.

items.title: iOS 7
items.notes: Controversial: Jony Ive's dramatic flat design overhaul, polarizing at launch.

items.title: iOS 8
items.notes: Third-party keyboards, widgets, app extensions, and HealthKit.

items.title: iOS 10
items.notes: SiriKit SDK, iMessage apps and stickers, redesigned notifications.

items.title: iOS 13
items.notes: System-wide Dark Mode, Sign in with Apple, SwiftUI debut.

items.title: iOS 14
items.notes: Home screen widgets, App Library, and picture-in-picture on iPhone.

items.title: iOS 16
items.notes: Customizable Lock Screen with widgets and Live Activities.

items.title: iOS 17
items.notes: StandBy mode, Journal app, NameDrop contact sharing.

items.title: iOS 18
items.notes: Apple Intelligence AI features, RCS messaging support, app locking.

items.title: Slackware
items.notes: The oldest surviving Linux distribution (1993), known for its simplicity and manual configuration.

items.title: Debian
items.notes: The universal operating system. Foundation for Ubuntu, Mint, and dozens of derivatives.

items.title: Red Hat / RHEL
items.notes: The enterprise Linux standard, now owned by IBM. Powers most corporate servers.

items.title: Fedora
items.notes: Red Hat's community cutting-edge distro, a testing ground for RHEL.

items.title: Ubuntu
items.notes: Canonical's user-friendly Linux that brought Linux to the mainstream desktop.

items.title: Linux Mint
items.notes: The most recommended Linux for Windows switchers, with the Cinnamon desktop.

items.title: Arch Linux
items.notes: The DIY rolling-release distro. 'I use Arch, btw.' Legendary wiki.

items.title: Manjaro
items.notes: User-friendly Arch-based distro with GUI installers and curated repos.

items.title: Pop!_OS
items.notes: System76's developer/gamer-focused Ubuntu derivative with excellent NVIDIA support.

items.title: Kali Linux
items.notes: Offensive Security's Debian-based distro for penetration testing and security research.

items.title: SteamOS
items.notes: Valve's Arch-based gaming OS powering the Steam Deck handheld.

items.title: Gentoo
items.notes: Source-based distro where you compile everything from source. Maximum customization.

items.title: Alpine Linux
items.notes: Ultra-lightweight musl-based distro, the default base image for Docker containers.

items.title: Raspberry Pi OS
items.notes: Debian-based OS for Raspberry Pi single-board computers.
